pamphlet_excerpts: Evidence That You Have Cared: Present evidence that you have cared: If you are not a pet owner and plan to buy or adopt ananimal to earn this merit badge, first give serious thought to pet ownership (p. 7).

Evidence That You Have Cared Principle 2: Present evidence that you have cared Principle 2: You must realize what every responsiblepet owner already knows: It takes time, effort, and money to care for a pet properly (p. 7).

Evidence That You Have Cared Principle 3: Present evidence that you have cared Principle 3: You must ensure quality health care for your pet, which could include vaccinations and preventive andemergency care as needed (p. 7).
Evidence That You Have Cared Principle 4: Present evidence that you have cared Principle 4: You must take the time to properlytrain your pet so that it does not become a nuisance (p. 7).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Evidence That You Have Cared): Step 1 (Present evidence that you have cared): You mustdedicate yourself to the well-being of a living animal, which means sometimes giving up other activities, such as TV, totend to your pet's (p. 7).
Step 2 (Evidence That You Have Cared): Step 2 (Present evidence that you have cared): Understand thatdifferent pets require different living arrangements (p. 7).
Step 3 (Evidence That You Have Cared): Step 3 (Present evidence that you have cared): Municipal laws may restrict the types of pets (p. 7).
Step 4 (Evidence That You Have Cared): Step 4 (Present evidence that you have cared): Give baby canaries all the egg food (available at pet stores) and conditioning food they want (p. 7).

Step 3 (Pet in A Pet Show): Step 3 (Your pet in a pet): If you decide todo this, enroll your dog once it has been vaccinated (p. 21).
Step 4 (Pet in A Pet Show): Step 4 (Your pet in a pet): Ask your veterinarian for help in picking a class that matches your dog's abilities (p. 21).

requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) Explore careers related to this merit badge. Research one career to learn about the training and education needed, costs, job prospects, salary, job duties, and career advancement. Your research methods may include, with your parent or guardian's permission, an internet or library search, an interview with a professional in the field, or a visit to a location where people in this career work. Discuss with your counselor both your findings and what about this profession might make it an interesting career. (b) Explore how you could use knowledge and skills from this merit badge to pursue a hobby or healthy lifestyle. Research any training needed, expenses, and organizations that promote or support it. Discuss with your counselor what short-term and long-term goals you might have if you pursued this. Resource: Animal Hobbies (video)
